definition.def: If there is a link between two things or situations, there is a relationship between them, for example because one thing causes or affects the other.
examples: ...the link between smoking and lung cancer. [+ between]

definition.def: If someone or something links two things or situations, there is a relationship between them, for example because one thing causes or affects the other.
examples: The U.N. Security Council has linked any lifting of sanctions to compliance with the ceasefire terms. [VERB noun + to]
The study further strengthens the evidence linking smoking with early death. [VERB noun to noun]
Liver cancer is linked to the hepatitis B virus. [VERB noun + to]
The detention raised two distinct but closely linked questions. [VERB-ed]

definition.def: A link between two things or places is a physical connection between them.
examples: ...the high-speed rail link between London and the Channel Tunnel. [+ between]
The new road schemes include a link between the two cities.
Stalin insisted that the radio link with the German Foreign Ministry should remain open. [+ with]

definition.def: If two places or objects are linked or something links them, there is a physical connection between them.
examples: ...the Rama Road, which links the capital, Managua, with the Caribbean coast. [V n + with/to]
The campus is linked by regular bus services to Coventry. [be V-ed + with/to]
...the Channel Tunnel linking Britain and France. [VERB noun]

definition.def: A link between two people, organizations, or places is a friendly or business connection between them.
examples: The university has close links with local employers. [+ with]
In 1984 the long link between AC Cars and the Hurlock family was severed. [+ between]
A cabinet minister came under investigation for links to the Mafia. [+ to]

definition.def: A link to another person or organization is something that allows you to communicate with them or have contact with them.
examples: She was my only link with the past.
The Red Cross was created to provide a link between soldiers in battle and their families at home.
These projects will provide vital links between companies and universities.

definition.def: If you link one person or thing to another, you claim that there is a relationship or connection between them.
examples: Criminologist Dr Ann Jones has linked the crime to social circumstances. [V n + to/with]
The tabloids have linked him with various women. [V n + to/with]
...a report in The Sunday Times linking him with organized crime. [V n to/with n]

definition.def: In computing, a link is a connection between different documents, or between different parts of the same document, using hypertext.
examples: Certainly, Andreessen didn't think up using hypertext to link Internet documents. [VERB noun]

definition.def: A link is one of the rings in a chain.
If you link one thing with another, you join them by putting one thing through the other.
examples: She linked her arm through his. [VERB noun preposition/adverb]
He linked the fingers of his hands together on his stomach. [VERB noun preposition/adverb]

definition.def: If two or more people link arms, or if one person links arms with another, they stand next to each other, and each person puts their arm round the arm of the person next to them.
examples: It was so slippery that some of the walkers linked arms and proceeded very carefully.
She stayed with them, linking arms with the two girls, joking with the boys.

definition.def: If you link up with someone, you join them for a particular purpose.
examples: They linked up with a series of local anti-nuclear and anti-apartheid groups. [VERB PARTICLE + with]
The Russian and American armies linked up for the first time on the banks of the river Elbe. [VERB PARTICLE]

definition.def: If one thing is linked up to another, the two things are connected to each other.
examples: The motion detectors were linked up to my laptop. [be V-ed P + to]
